findings.title: Client handoff closes the old socket before defining where an in-flight tool result goes
findings.evidence: "The add-in sends a Close frame to the current client." ... "If a command is currently executing on the UI thread, the add-in holds the new connection in a pending state... until the command completes." ... "Once the executing command completes... the new connection proceeds with the handshake"
findings.problem: The spec starts the close handshake with the current client before the executing command finishes, but does not define how the command's eventual ToolResultMessage is delivered. The old client is being closed, and the new client is not yet upgraded.
findings.why_it_matters: A tool can mutate the model and complete successfully while no connection is eligible to receive its result, leaving the client with an unobserved state transition and ambiguous dedup/retry behavior.
findings.proposed_fix: Define one explicit rule for this handoff case: either delay sending Close until the executing command result is sent, or mark the call Abandoned and require replay to the new client after handshake, or reject the new connection with a busy/retry response.

findings.title: `default_mm` and `default_inch` do not map to distinct template-resolution mechanisms
findings.evidence: "Supported templates: \"default_mm\", \"default_inch\"." ... "Read the default part template path from SolidWorks user preferences (ISldWorks.GetUserPreferenceStringValue(swDefaultTemplatePart))." ... "After creation, set the document unit system"
findings.problem: Both symbolic template names resolve through the same single `swDefaultTemplatePart` path. The only difference defined is a post-creation unit switch, which does not make them distinct templates.
findings.why_it_matters: If template content differs beyond units (custom properties, starting geometry, standards, document settings), the API contract is false and callers cannot reliably request the intended base document.
findings.proposed_fix: Either define separate configured paths/preferences for mm and inch templates, or rename the parameter to represent requested units and document that the same default template file is reused.

findings.title: Raw `CallId` is used in screenshot filenames without a stated server-side validation step
findings.problem: The file path incorporates client-supplied `callId`, but this spec does not require the adapter to validate or sanitize that value before using it as a filesystem path component.
findings.why_it_matters: Any local process that can connect to the localhost WebSocket can supply malformed path content, causing invalid filenames or path traversal outside the intended screenshot directory.
findings.proposed_fix: Reject any inbound `CallId` that is not a strict UUIDv7/lowercase match before registry or file-path use, or stop using client-supplied identifiers directly in filenames.

findings.title: The screenshot permission model contradicts its own validation procedure
findings.evidence: Section 7.2: "The orchestrator is read-only." Section 7.4: "The orchestrator validates that this path is readable ... by creating and deleting a temporary file."
findings.problem: A create/delete probe requires write permission, which contradicts the stated read-only role for the orchestrator.
findings.why_it_matters: A directory that is correctly readable but not writable will be treated as invalid, and implementers will not know which permission model to honor.
findings.proposed_fix: Either change the ownership model to grant orchestrator write/delete access, or replace the validation with a read-only check that does not require writing.

findings.title: Client-side screenshot-path validation has no defined mechanism to change add-in behavior
findings.evidence: "If validation fails, the orchestrator logs a warning and disables screenshot-dependent features for the session; screenshot capture is omitted from tool results." Handshake defines only add-in -> client `AddinReadyMessage`.
findings.problem: The path validation decision happens on the orchestrator side, but no message or negotiated capability is defined to tell the add-in to omit screenshot data from future tool results.
findings.why_it_matters: This creates an implementation gap: either the add-in keeps emitting screenshot fields anyway, or the orchestrator must silently invent its own rule to avoid calling screenshot-dependent tools.
findings.proposed_fix: Specify one mechanism: either the orchestrator must stop sending screenshot-related tool calls, or add a negotiated capability/error message that disables screenshot emission in the add-in for the session.

findings.title: `ModifyParameter` does not define how `featureId` interacts with `parameterName`
findings.evidence: Signature: `void ModifyParameter(string featureId, string parameterName, double newValue);` Comment: "ParameterName MUST be the concrete SolidWorks parameter identifier (e.g., 'Depth@Boss-Extrude1')"
findings.problem: A concrete parameter identifier already embeds the owning feature name, but the API also requires a separate `featureId` and does not say what happens when they disagree.
findings.why_it_matters: Different implementations can ignore `featureId`, use it as a secondary lookup, or throw on mismatch, leading to incompatible behavior and possible edits to the wrong parameter.
findings.proposed_fix: Either remove `featureId` from the method, or define exact validation and failure behavior when `featureId` and `parameterName` identify different features.

findings.title: `AddinSessionId` lifecycle is contradictory for add-in reloads inside one SolidWorks process
findings.evidence: Section 8.1: input is "guaranteed to change on add-in reload". Section 8.2: "Stable for the duration of the SolidWorks session" and regenerated "On SolidWorks restart".
findings.problem: These statements conflict when the add-in is unloaded and reloaded without restarting SolidWorks. The spec does not say whether that is the same session or a new one.
findings.why_it_matters: Reconnect logic, stale-epoch detection, state-version scoping, and registry clearing all depend on a precise definition of the session boundary.
findings.proposed_fix: Explicitly define add-in reload behavior within the same SolidWorks process and align registry/session-reset semantics and tests to that rule.

findings.title: The UI-thread dispatch bootstrap has no defined product behavior if the injected `WindowsFormsSynchronizationContext` does not work
findings.evidence: Section 2.2: "If no `SynchronizationContext` is installed ... the add-in installs a `WindowsFormsSynchronizationContext`". Section 11: "confirm post/dispatch round-trip works."
findings.problem: The spec relies on a manually installed WinForms synchronization context as the core dispatch mechanism, but only defines a Day-0 check, not runtime failure handling or a fallback if the probe fails on a target machine.
findings.why_it_matters: If this bootstrap is invalid on some SolidWorks hosts, every COM call path becomes unsafe and the adapter has no defined startup failure mode.
findings.proposed_fix: Make the dispatch probe a mandatory startup gate with explicit failure handling (refuse to start the bridge/add-in and emit a deterministic error), or specify a fallback marshalling mechanism that does not depend on this context injection.

findings.title: `ToolInProgress` cleanup on exception is not required
findings.evidence: "`ToolInProgress` flag (set by `ToolDispatcher` before and after each tool execution). While `ToolInProgress` is true, incoming SW events are noted but state capture is suppressed"
findings.problem: The spec says the flag is set before and after execution, but does not require a `finally` path when tool execution throws.
findings.why_it_matters: One exception can leave event-driven state capture suppressed indefinitely, breaking later state-version updates and reconnect comparisons.
findings.proposed_fix: Require `ToolDispatcher` to set/reset `ToolInProgress` in a `try/finally` block and add a build-breaking test for exception paths.

top_3_must_fix: Define legal result-delivery behavior during active-client handoff in Section 6.1.
Fix `NewPart` so `default_mm` and `default_inch` map to distinct mechanisms or rename the API to represent units only.
Validate or sanitize `CallId` before using it in screenshot filenames.
